notes.title: Update v.0.8.2: Enemy Capital Ships
notes.content:
[h2][b]Hi there friends,[/b][/h2][p]🏴‍☠️🏴‍☠️ The Pirate Patrol [b]v.0.8.2-Alpha[/b] update has been released! [/p][p]With this update, the long-awaited [b]enemy capital warships[/b] are finally entering the game. But that's not all; the update also brings significant innovations to the game's dynamics. We'll go over them one by one:[/p][hr][/hr][h2]🚨 Enemy Capital Warships 🚨[/h2][p]First, let's talk about the enemy capital warships. These are [b]extremely dangerous enemy vessels[/b]. They can destroy your fighter ships in a matter of seconds and inflict heavy damage on "The FATHER" in a short period. The turrets on these ships are comprised of [b]high-damage turbo laser weapons[/b] and can rotate very quickly. This means they can rapidly destroy incoming fighter ships and missiles.[/p][p]Therefore, if you intend to attack enemy Capital ships with your fighters, we highly recommend planning this operation with a [b]large attack team[/b]. If you consider 3-4-5 fighters attacking an enemy capital ship simultaneously, along with the missiles they launch, you can create a window of opportunity to damage the main ship by reducing the risk of the enemy's deadly turrets focusing on a single target.[/p][p]You can also target the [b]turrets on the enemy capital ships[/b]. Every "tooth" you destroy will result in less damage when the enemy tries to bite you. We also recommend watching this video about Capital Ship battles.[/p][p][/p][previewyoutube="5tNSSl1z9Rk;full"][/previewyoutube][h2]🪐 Removing Planet Blockades 🌎 🪐🌕🌑☄️[/h2][p]Planets on the galaxy map are now under [b]Autonex blockade[/b], recognizable by the [b]"red" ring[/b] around them. If you reach a planet, clear all orbiting Autonex ships, and then leave the area, the planet will be freed from the blockade and symbolized by a [b]"green" ring[/b]. These details are important because planets that are either freed or still under enemy blockade will have different effects on the game. For example, in this update, this will be noticeable in [b]Refueling[/b]...[/p][hr][/hr][h2]⛽ Refueling and Autonex Ambush [/h2][p]With the previous update, if you ran out of fuel while moving across the Galaxy map, you could call a tanker ship from the nearest planet to refuel you. Now, [b]enemy Autonex scouts can break into these tankers' communication channels and track their routes to find your location[/b].[/p][p]This means that as the tanker approaches to refuel you, you might suddenly be attacked by a [b]heavy Autonex hunter team[/b]. During this "Fuel" mission, you must [b]protect the tanker[/b] attempting to refuel you from enemy fire. Otherwise, not only will refueling fail, but you'll also suffer a significant loss of prestige, and the cost of refueling again later will [b]dramatically increase[/b].

If this fuel tanker originates from a planet under [b]enemy blockade[/b], the likelihood of Autonex scouts detecting your location will increase. Tankers coming from [b]freed planets[/b] have a lower risk of being tracked by the Autonex.[/p][p][/p][hr][/hr][h2]🍀 Random Encounters 🤞[/h2][p]Of course, no RPG is complete without "Random Encounters"! 😉[/p][p]We now have enough in-game dynamics to create [b]Random Encounters[/b]. So, as you traverse the Galaxy map, you might experience some encounters that pop up randomly.[/p][p]For now, these encounters will feature [b]Autonex hunters[/b]. These are task forces with heavy firepower, and their sole objective is to destroy The Father. They will also include [b]heavily armed capital ships[/b]. If you feel you won't be able to destroy this heavy assault team, and if Captain Lionheart's Bridge Console has the [b]Hyperjump application[/b], you can try jumping directly to the Galaxy map from your current location without reaching a Gravity Escape Point.[/p][p]Alternatively, you might have the [b]Full Speed application[/b] among your Officer console applications, or you might have added a [b]Trait Skill[/b] that speeds up The Father to the captain's character traits. Additionally, your Engineer or Tactic officer's console might have [b]hacker applications that freeze the enemy for a certain period[/b]... You can choose to escape this formidable enemy by combining the different options at your disposal. As you know, the tactical combinations you can use in Pirate Patrol's tactical battles are limited only by your creativity! [/p][p][b]A Small Note:[/b] As far as we can calculate, it's possible to execute over [b]650,000 different tactical operations[/b] within the Tactical Map just by varying [b]Officer applications and Captain trait skills[/b]. When we add factors like pilot abilities, fighter weapon selections, and the main ship's weapon and missile options, the number of tactical choices you can employ against the enemy in Pirate Patrol reaches into the [b]billions[/b].[/p][p]In future updates, we plan to include different types of [b]Random Encounters[/b], such as "lost ship debris" and "merchant ships selling advanced equipment," or a mission to rescue a [b]fighter pilot adrift in space[/b]. We're open to your suggestions on this![/p][p][/p][hr][/hr][h2]Improvements in the Settings Section[/h2][p]Players requested several improvements for the [b]Settings section[/b], and these are now available. Here's what's changed in Settings:[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43756138/c14cdd7f248d2820ded72cc332bc184587e0f7cc.jpg"][/img][/p][p][/p][h2]⏸️ Toggling Smart Pause On/Off[/h2][p]Some of our players requested the ability to toggle the [b]Smart Pause feature[/b] on and off via the settings. You can now find this option in the [b]Settings menu[/b].[/p][p][/p][h2]📣 Pilot Voice Settings[/h2][p]You now have a separate volume setting for pilot radio calls during combat. This way, you can more easily hear these vital transmissions, even if you turn down other sound effects.[/p][p][/p][h2]⌨️Enhanced Keymap[/h2][p]Ther e's now an [b]enhanced and easier-to-understand keymap[/b] that visually displays the key assignments on your keyboard.[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43756138/4bbf6a9f252a1cbdbd8af1a6f5283b9e4218b3d5.jpg"][/img][/p][p][/p][h2]🛠️ Save System Bugs Fixed[/h2][p]We noticed that in some cases, players were unable to [b]load[/b] their games from within the game and had to return to the main menu. This bug has now been [b]fixed[/b].[/p][p]
[/p][hr][/hr][p]Beyond these, we've also implemented some [b]minor bug fixes[/b] and [b]graphics/sound improvements[/b].[/p][p][/p][p]Thank you very much for your support of Pirate Patrol. If you'd like to help our development efforts by sharing information about Pirate Patrol with your friends on social media, we'd be thrilled![/p][p][/p][p]Have fun! [/p]

notes.title: v.0.8 is out! Major Update!
notes.content:
With the release of version 0.8, Pirate Patrol players now have access to a significantly expanded array of new features.

 Here’s a quick rundown:

[list]
[*] [b]Recruit New Pilots and Officers:[/b] You can now add fresh pilots and officers to your fleet.
[*] [b]Acquire New Fighterships:[/b] Strengthen your fleet by purchasing a variety of new warships.
[*] [b]Character Progression (Player & NPC):[/b] Level up both your own character and your NPC (officers and pilots) characters.
[*] [b]Skill Selections:[/b] Choose from new skills (Applications) for both your player character and your NPCs.
[*] [b]Officer Consoles and Tactical Applications:[/b] Gain more control and strategic depth through officer consoles.
[*] [b]Main Ship Level Upgrades:[/b] Enhance your main ship's capabilities by upgrading its level.
[*] [b]Signal Anomalies and Exploration on Tactical Map:[/b] Discover new opportunities by exploring signal anomalies on the tactical map.
[*] [b]Heavy Damage and Personel Loss:[/b] Space conflicts are now much more realistic. 
[*]  [b]Reputation System:[/b] Now, your choices affect your reputation.
[*]  [b]Mission Details:[/b] 
[*] [b]Animation Updates:[/b] Enjoy improved in-game animations.
[*] [b]Save and Load Functionality:[/b] You can now save your game and load it whenever you wish.
[*] [b]Battle Report: [/b] At the end of the battle, you will receive a comprehensive situation report. 
[*] [b]Galaxy map fuel mechanism:[/b] Your mothership is running out of fuel and you need to refuel.
[*] [b]QOL improvements:[/b] 
[/list]

Here is the important details:

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43756138/3c82267e70d4eda8f169a1089351a0d2aabbce81.jpg[/img]

 [b]Recruit New Pilots and Officers[/b]

You will now be able to find new pilots and officers on all space stations and planets. Each NPC has different skills and levels, of course. Accordingly, contract prices and salary payments will also differ. If you no longer want an officer or pilot on your crew, you can dismiss them at a station or planet. Keep in mind that when you dismiss a crew member, you must pay them severance.  Pirate Patrol might be the first and only video game in which you have to compensate a crew member when firing them. In our 45 years of gaming experience, we have never come across such a detail.

[b]Acquire New Fighterships:[/b] 

You start the game with one fightership, one officer, and one pilot. As you must find new pilots and officers, you must also find new fighters for your mother ship. You can find these ships in the planet or station trade panels. However, you will notice that each ship has different features and prices. These advanced combat vehicles are expensive and hard to find due to their high prices. Therefore, you should manage your budget correctly.


[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43756138/3c4eb1759ea84e689c3717ae61bea00015d3e695.jpg[/img]

[b]Character Progression[/b]

Players can now upgrade the main character and NPCs by gaining experience.  Captain Lionheart and his officers earn upgrade points as he levels up. Officers and pilots can use their upgrade points in the Hangar window. As they level up and improve their skills, officers can run tactical applications on the Officer Console more efficiently.

Pilots gain experience by flying in space and participating in combat. You can see the pilots' experience level under their profile picture.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43756138/3201c4e6d85c66dcd8a31cbf4a1d1247134879c6.jpg[/img]

Captain Lionheart's skills are controlled from the "Character" screen, which can be accessed with the "P" key. There, you can upgrade Captain Lionheart's character traits. If the conditions are right, you can select skis from the skill list and start using them. Some of these skills are passive, while others are active. To activate active skis, press the relevant icon under the bridge panel on the tactical map.


[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43756138/39b77809c38d8db0fddcec99d35a81007b03199c.jpg[/img]

[b]Officer Consoles and Tactical Applications:[/b]

Officers can execute different tactical operations through consoles on the bridge. The “apps” that run on these consoles can be found by exploring space or bought through trade. However, you cannot sell these tactical applications.


[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43756138/375f80bfa287a35d801796d2634932a965232f25.jpg[/img]

[b]Main Ship Level Upgrades:[/b]
As you level up, you will be able to upgrade the mothership's armor, fuel tank, crew capacity, logistics storage and energy output.

If you run out of fuel, you won't be able to move around the galaxy map. The more crew you lose, the slower your ship will move. When your logistics depot is empty, your guns won't have bullets, and your engineers and technicians won't be able to repair damage to the ship. It's important to have enough energy output to power the internal equipment you add to the ship.


[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43756138/774b5a1f7b856f3e59ed48e0721a170e66669ee4.jpg[/img]

[b]Signal Anomalies and Exploration on Tactical Map:[/b]

There are now more details to explore on the tactical map. By scanning these signal anomalies, you can uncover secrets hidden in the area. However, keep in mind that the more your fighters run their scanners, the easier it is for the enemy to detect your location and attack.


[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43756138/7267a7e282587051c566e1f6e341051e7251aaf3.jpg[/img]

[b]Heavy Damage and Personel Loss:[/b]

Space conflicts are now much more realistic. As your mother ship takes damage, holes appear in its hull. Until the damage is repaired, flames and armor fragments will fly out of these openings into space. This is not just a visual effect, though. When your mother ship starts to take heavy damage, every enemy shot that hits the ship can result in casualties. There may be fatalities among the crew. The fighter ships stationed in the hangar may be damaged, and the officers you have painstakingly leveled up or the skilled pilots preparing for a flight in the hangar may die as a result of enemy fire.


[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43756138/52d7bfd77c6927374d6551b5f9295abd292abbaa.png[/img]

[b]Reputation System[/b]

Your choices will now directly affect your reputation. Your reputation will be impacted by the missions you respond to, the civilian ships you save from the enemy on the tactical map, and the civilians you fail to save in order to protect yourself. With a low reputation level (BRUTAL), you will be known as a commander who uses harsh and brutal tactics. Conversely, you will be known as a hero (MERCIFUL), someone who cares more about the lives of civilians than anything else and tries to protect them at the risk of his own life. These levels of reputation will impact the game in various ways, including the salaries of the NPCs you work with, the prices you pay in trade, and the equipment you can access.


[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43756138/2ff5c2e073093a4fb6f7399985f19a5bbf0020dd.jpg[/img]

[b]Mission Details[/b] 
Now, when you hover your mouse over a mission on the galaxy map, you will be able to see the details of the mission and the prestige points it will award. In future updates, other details such as cash rewards or equipment rewards will also be available in these popup windows.

notes.title: Work in progress: Officer Console Softwares
notes.content:
Hello friends, we are nearing the end of the [b]Officer Skills Update[/b] that we have been working on. We have created a "Work in Progress" video for this new feature that we will be adding to the game, and we would like to ask players how we can further improve the system and get feedback before we finalize it.

First of all, it should be said that we designed these "skills" as "[b]softwares[/b]", which is slightly different from the classic definition of "skill" in RPG games and more in line with the [b]science fiction [/b]theme. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43756138/a257de792bf750b37a70a49eff8ace5d2ee2d421.jpg[/img]

There are consoles on the bridge of the mother ship that each officer controls, and we have defined the "skills" in the game as "softwares" [b]installed [/b]on these consoles. 


[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43756138/acb10736c2f86e036c6eefe79aac26906a2228a3.jpg[/img]

Practically speaking, we can also define this software as algorithms that make it easier for the officers to [b]create new tactics[/b] on the battlefield by intervening and [b]manipulating [/b]various procedures of the mother ship. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43756138/bc5149e228677526f819ae32b557b80ae1d5e6ec.jpg[/img]

During the game, the player can gain new "abilities" by installing the necessary software onto the console. Of course, different "softwares" can be found on different space stations and planets in the game. Or, if the player [b]scans [/b]the wreckage of a space ship or space station, they will have the opportunity to find different/surprising softwares.

[previewyoutube=FDfpDQXtoPI;full][/previewyoutube]

On the other hand, not every software will work on every consoles. Softwares are divided into 4 categories: "Captain", "XO", "Tactical Officer", "Engineer Officer"... Of course, the effectiveness of each software will give results related to the level and personal skills of each officer.

[h3][b]So how will console software affect the game?[/b][/h3]

It may be more useful to answer this question by using an [b]example [/b]to explain the tactical richness and [b]endless combinations[/b] that these abilities bring to the game: In this picture, for example, we can see that the third software on Captain Lionheart's console is called [b]"BURN'em ALL".[/b]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43756138/e24b68cb6a994a58cce67017d7506c6f06db3ba4.jpg[/img]

When this ability is active, the captain overloads the [b]mothership's engines,[/b] causing them to emit a great deal of heat and radiation. As a result, enemy ships attempting to attack the Mothership [b]from the rear[/b] will take heavy damage when they enter the rear area, which has become a [b]"death trap"[/b] due to the searing heat and radiation emitted by the engines.

Additionally, by simultaneously activating one of the Tactical Officer's abilities, [b]Missile Barrage[/b], you can hit these enemy ships with special missiles filled with [b]very high amounts of explosives[/b], causing damage to the enemy's internal equipment/engines and [b]slowing [/b]them down. In this case, they will move much [b]slower [/b]in the "death trap" behind the ship, [b]staying [/b]in the area [b]longer [/b]and taking even more damage.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43756138/dd89033b15cfdb8c4a598d6140781115ec9f9640.jpg[/img]

In the currently released version (v.0.7g), you have the opportunity to try [b]12 softwares[/b] on the Bridge panel. In addition, 50 softwares are ready for release, but we plan to prepare [b]100+ softwares [/b]before the update, and new surprise softwares will probably be added to the game in updates after the game is released.

Of course, when the player starts the game, each officer will have a maximum of 1 software installed on their console, and these will be the most basic level softwares. 

However, as the player travels through the galaxy and levels up, they will have the chance to find [b]more advanced[/b] softwares, and while they save them for their [b]inventory[/b], they will have the opportunity to change the installed software on the consoles whenever they want.

If you have a chance to try this new "[b]Officer Console Softwares"[/b] system, we would love to hear your feedback.

Have fun : )

notes.title: Update v.0.7d: Small Bug Fixes and minor surprises
notes.content:
Hi Friends,

-Some minor bugs have been fixed.
-The tutorial page for Scan and Loot was missing in the old version, it has been added to the “How To Play” section.

[h3][b]-Neural Network Tactical Speed bonus[/b][/h3]
Now Neural Network not only speeds up or slows down the game, but also provides bonuses to the player. When you set the Neural Network to the “Slow” or “Tactical” speed setting, this technically means that the brain and body functions of your entire crew and pilots will reach a speed that can compete with artificial intelligence. As a player, you may find the tactical map “slowed down”, but on the battlefield, your tiny NPCs have gained a significant advantage over the AI. They can target the enemy better, they can hit more critical/sensitive points of the enemy and so on: 

[olist]
[*] With Slow Speed, all your weapons do [b]x1.5 more damage.[/b]
[*] With Tactical Speed, all your weapons do [b]x2 more damage.[/b]
[/olist]

Neural Network is now closer to its purpose in the story.


[h3][b]-Started testing new features[/b][/h3]
[b]Officer skills[/b] will go live shortly. We are preparing hundreds of new skills for officers and pilots. But before we go live with this major update, we wanted to see a small test live... 

For now, you can only see the first 3 abilities of the [b]XO[/b] on The Bridge Panel. The first two of these abilities are currently active for testing purposes.

notes.title: QOL improvements: Object comparisons and enemy information card
notes.content:
Players will now be able to [b]compare[/b] both the objects they find in space and the objects they examine for purchase in the market with the equipment used on the mothership and fighters. 

Since both the mothership and the fighters have [b]a lot of equipment installed[/b] on them, we didn't want to create an extra challenging mechanism for the player to choose which equipment they want to compare. 

In the comparison system, whichever object the player is examining, the characteristics of the “same type” of objects installed on the ship will [b]automatically [/b]appear on the screen. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43756138/b0ab69078ace105f8b5b54a3c90cbbc3b041639a.jpg[/img]

[h3][b]Enemy information card[/b][/h3]

An [b]informational card[/b] about the enemy ship will now appear on the tactical map when the player hovers the cursor over enemy ships. This card will show the enemy's:

[list]
[*] Type
[*] Level
[*] HP
[*] Speed
[*] Threat factor
[*] Firepower
[/list]

Also, with next update, you will see the [b]bounties[/b] for eliminate that enemy. Yes, we are preparing the [b]bounty[/b] system for enemies, it will be active in the next update.

This information card will also show which friendly ship the enemy ship is [b]targeting[/b]. This way, when you want to come to the aid of friendly ships in distress, you will be able to more quickly determine which enemy ships you should attack first. 

For example, when a fighter ship with a very [b]low HP[/b] and its pilot asks for help, you can target the enemy ships targeting it with your other fighter ships, turrets and [b]mother ship missiles[/b] to relieve your pilot and buy time until it returns to the mothership. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43756138/bd3ad47692c9d6d469b6527f1530b9b23b9c126e.jpg[/img]

[h3][b]What is the difference between Threat Factor and Firepower?
[/b][/h3]
The value you see with the sword symbol on the information card is the “Threat Factor” of the enemy ship, while the bullet symbol just below it indicates its Firepower. 

[b]Firepower[/b] indicates the potential damage that the enemy ship's weapons will inflict on the player when firing at the player. For example, if this value is 10, the enemy ship has the potential to deal 10 points of damage to you. However, this value may vary depending on the pilot's defense skills, the skills of your officers, and the defense equipment you use on the mother ship. This damage can take values of 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9, 10, etc. every time the enemy fires and scores a hit.  In other words, the enemy's damage to you depends on the enemy's firepower and your defensive capabilities.

[b]Threat Factor[/b] is a value that helps both the player (you) and the AI fighter pilots make [b]tactical decisions[/b] when choosing targets. It is calculated based on the enemy ship's HP, Level, firepower, speed and type. 

Enemy ships with a high Threat Factor can be much more dangerous, meaning they can be very formidable opponents. They can inflict heavy damage on you during combat. These values, calculated and reported by your [b]Tactical Officer[/b] on the mothership, in a sense help all friendly units on the battlefield to select targets and determine combat tactics.

***
Have fun...

notes.title: Update v.0.7: Neural Network
notes.content:
Player control over the Neural Network, one of the most strategic features of Pirate Patrol, has now reached its final form. 

By swapping out the mother ship's Neural Network Chip, players can upgrade this network to suit their needs. 

[b]Neural Network Chips[/b] can be found in the wreckage of enemy ships or other debris in space. They can also be bought and sold on trading stations and planets.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43756138/b89f45bd0396e8b283182dca66c3ec10bcb76f86.jpg[/img]

These chips have 3 main variables. These variables are

[b]1. Neural network capacity: [/b]
Determines the running time of the network. The higher this value is, the longer you can run the neural network without interruption.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43756138/b5d4d5208b07e5a418b170dd30ebc5fb7033c7e5.jpg[/img]

[b]2. Network Normalization Speed: [/b]
Your ability to use the neural network depends on your crew's mental and physical ability to withstand the strain of the network. This value symbolizes the speed at which the crew's mental and physical readings return to normal after the network has been run. The higher the value, the faster the Nural Network will normalize and "get back on track".


[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43756138/3a70d76f1b7a9a486308bcb0e9fad6a523d93167.jpg[/img]
[b]3. Energy Consumption:[/b]
This value, like all other major ship equipment, indicates the amount of energy consumed by the chip. If the total energy consumed by all the ship's equipment is greater than the energy produced by the ship's reactors, you will not be able to use that equipment. You must either replace other high energy consuming equipment with low energy consuming items, or replace the ship's reactor modulator with a model that produces more energy.

***

[h3][b]-Improvements:[/b][/h3]
You will now see color codes on the left side of items on the main ship configuration screen and at trading stations. These color codes make it easier to tell which item is which at a glance, making it easier to keep track of inventories that can grow to hundreds of items in later stages.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43756138/9d5e94d0de631c2b0ff1d7c83a0ab9d58444cfb8.jpg[/img]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43756138/b43f0f1e3b6f1ff7367f0c96718e0a00162a4535.jpg[/img]

notes.title: A brief example of NPC A.I.
notes.content:
The video below shows two NPC fighters (Tiger and Patch) on a mission to take out corporatocracy-backed robot pirates attacking civilian ships.

This short video is a good example of how the NPC AI works in Pirate Patrol.

[previewyoutube=pHFbcLXiYkc;full][/previewyoutube]

The robot fighter group consists of 10 ships, including high-level robots with high firepower. The NPC fighters only have level 3 ships. You can see that the robot pirates have level 4 ships.

The commander (you) in The FATHER equips these NPCs with powerful weapons before they go on a mission. One fighter has a rare (pink) weapon with high firepower. The other NPC's weapon has half the firepower.

[b][h3]High firepower of the enemy
[/h3][/b]
The high-level robots in the group of enemies are extremely dangerous because their armour is very durable and their firepower is formidable, and if two of them get together and coordinate their attacks, they can destroy NPC fighters in seconds, their weapons are powerful enough to pierce the armour of NPC fighters like paper. 

If you look at the fighter panel on the left in the video, you can see that the HP of the NPC fighters (Tiger) is halved after just one or two hits. If they take one or two more hits, they are easily defeated.

NPC fighters acting as wingmen are under the control of artificial intelligence. In other words, they select targets and determine the dogfight algorithm without player intervention. The NPCs are aware of the 'two against ten' situation, and in this case they will split up to prevent the crowded enemy group from concentrating their firepower, choose easy targets that they can eliminate quickly, and destroy them quickly. When they realise they cannot escape enemy fire, they will abandon the dogfight and perform evasive manoeuvres, and once out of the line of fire, they will regroup and continue to attack the enemy from different angles.

These fully AI controlled NPCs 'raid' the robot fighters that are busy attacking civilian ships, mowing down 10 ships in just 2 minutes without allowing them to take ground and defend, then returning to the mother ship (The FATHER).

[h3][b]Analysis of results
[/b][/h3]
This case study proves that we do not need to fly our huge mother ship and 5 NPC fighters at the same time during missions, attacking enemy groups with all our might. With rational planning, fighters equipped with the right gear and used by the right pilots can easily deal with large groups of enemy robots.

Moreover, because we operate with a small and low-profile attack group, our risk of being ambushed by the enemy is reduced. When we move the giant mother ship and a large number of NPC fighters alongside it, the large waves of motion and signals created in space create enough opportunity for the Corporatocracy robots that are looking for us everywhere to notice, detect, and attack us.

[h3][b]Tactical control is always in your hands
[/b][/h3]
On the other hand, if you send your pilots on a mission away from the main ship, the commanders in the command room (you and your officers) have to make sure that they complete the mission successfully.

One of the details that will catch your attention in the video is that both NPC fighters (Patch and Tiger) have permission to use turbo weapons... This is understandable, as they went on a raid to fight 10 strong enemies. The faster they fire, the faster they can complete the raid and return without giving the enemy a chance to group up. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43756138/74619c2ec6754740bc76c1706ad82cd7552ac07e.jpg[/img]

However, you may notice that the "bullet count" you see on the turbo fire button flows like water from a faucet. Fighters who start the fight with 500 bullets will have their bullet counts reduced to 398 and 250 by the end of the fight. Because of the weapon's lower damage effect on the Tiger's ship, the Tiger uses half of its ammunition to eliminate its enemies. Half the ammunition is used up in just 2 minutes of combat. If the battle had lasted another 2 minutes, and the Tiger had not been able to kill all the enemies with a few inaccurate shots, it would have run out of ammunition in a dangerous group of enemies.

This is where your influence and that of your officers comes into play. As a commander, you should sometimes limit the turbo-fire authority of your pilots who have a low hit rate and burn bullets like water, and you should tactically direct your fighters by checking details such as the number of bullets, missiles, and fuel status.

On the other hand, the soon-to-be-activated officers will be able to help the fighter pilots with their skills. For example, a talented Engineering Officer will be able to reduce fuel consumption by 10% by making the engines of the fighters work more effectively. 

Or a talented tactical officer will be able to increase the ammunition capacity of your fighters by 20%, and your fighters will be able to start the battle with 600 bullets instead of 500.

We think that this little information will give you an idea of where the game is going.

***

We would love to hear your thoughts and suggestions about the game, please share your thoughts with us. 
Thank you for supporting Early Access.

notes.title: Armour and Tutorial Update
notes.content:
The v0.6.5 update introduces a new factor to the game, armour detail. You can now replace the main ship's security system, the Armor Frequency Regulator Chip, with new models and control the amount of damage the main ship takes.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43756138/ac7f06a3cba4684cf92cd02e35b724ea2d22c89f.jpg[/img]

The Armor Frequency Regulator Chip generates vibrations at a subatomic level that reduce the effect of incoming fire on the main ship's special alloy armour. These chips of varying quality can be found in loot drops and trade stations throughout the game.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43756138/6a580c90f744cc2764083bf3fd05ed5012a81847.jpg[/img]

[b]"How to Play" Section
[/b]

As Pirate Patrol continues to grow in tactical depth and detail, we recognise that our players need practical and easy-to-understand gameplay support.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43756138/765e48564e30b15f9969b5ae02e1fbd96d2c77f8.jpg[/img]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43756138/b4fc21018bd0240a744a945e87bcce375e4c4353.jpg[/img]

Thanks to the "How to Play" section, which we have placed in the main menu at the start of the game and in the "Settings" menu, where it is easily accessible at any time during the game, players will be able to easily learn how to do what in the game with the help of explanations placed on the screenshots. These informative screens can be played back and forth by clicking on the arrows.
In addition, those who wish to revisit the information in the tutorial screens can access the tutorial information they missed in the 'Tutorial Screen' tab in the 'How to Play' section.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43756138/f7e0cec0b4f8ef8e8f31629fb6a1c3a034b91dba.jpg[/img]

[b]Changes to Fighter Launches and Preparations
[/b]
A quick note... During the Early Access process, we noticed that many of our friends were complaining about fighters not responding to the "launch" command during the 2-3 second preparation process, as we could not clearly explain to our players why fighters were launched with a delay and not "simultaneously".

In fact, our goal here was to shorten or lengthen the fighter preparation times depending on the effectiveness of the ship's engineering and logistics operations and the skills of the officers involved, thus increasing the RPG depth of the game.

There is also a very successful short video explaining what we mean:
[previewyoutube=81Q0ElGtToE;full][/previewyoutube]

However, as we have not yet implemented officer skill trees in the game, players have to endure the maximum preparation time for fighter preparation .

In order not to spoil the fun for our players at this stage of Early Access, we have reduced fighter preparation times to zero. As a result, you can now send all 5 fighters into space from the launch tubes at the same time.


[b]Bug Fixes[/b]
[list]
[*] Fixed a crash that could occur when dropping a missile into the turret slot on the weapons/equipment change screen of the mothership.

[*] Fixed a bug that was resetting the weapon blueprint in the deployable turret tower after mission completion.

[*] Fixed a bug that prevented fighter weapons and missiles from dealing damage to enemies based on their stats.

[*] A number of minor bugs have been fixed that were interfering with the smooth running of the game.
[/list]

Your comments and feedback are very helpful and valuable to us. Thank you for supporting Pirate Patrol during Early Access.

notes.title: Update v.0.6.4e: Deployable Turrets and Battle Report
notes.content:
In last week's news announcement, we talked about deployable turrets. Now these powerful tactical tools have arrived in the game.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43756138/2bd1e51268fe6ca3fe4fe069aaf14ae3182c2717.gif[/img]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43756138/ee7e09fb79429cf9a45cd255308d4d59ece316d7.png[/img]

To use Deployable Turrets, you can open the Bridge console at the top left of the screen, click on the Father icon and select the Turret from the menu that appears, or simply press 'R' and the Turret Deployment tool will open.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43756138/738eaced2ce82a446c568904b24f278ed396d7bc.png[/img]

Here you can deploy turrets within the area indicated by the green circle.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43756138/eff31629d2ec7d810fef4ccd8ba9ac2d491eb89f.png[/img]

Below the turret icon is the cost of the deployable turret you have selected. When you deploy the turret into space, this cost will be deducted from your resources.


[b][h3]You can use different turret models
[/h3][/b]
You can also choose which 'mini-turret' model you want to use to build a deployable turret in The Father's configuration screen. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43756138/357e041b8fbf0cc57727fbb702a9046a0c3f1aaa.jpg[/img]

You can do this by dropping the mini-turrets in your cargo onto the Deployable Turret box, or by left-clicking on one of the mini-turrets you used on The Father.

You will notice that each turret has a different cost. Obviously, more powerful turrets will cost more.

[h3]Deployable Turrets are not indestructible
[/h3]

Deployable turrets can be damaged and destroyed by enemy fire and by impacts from hovering asteroids. Therefore, we recommend that you think strategically when placing them.

Each turret has 500 bullets in its cartridge, and you should also bear in mind that it cannot fire any more once it runs out of bullets. It is not possible to collect these turrets or replenish their ammunition. 

However, when officers come into the equation in the future, we will find that some officers have abilities such as collecting turrets from space or replenishing ammunition. Let's keep this information a secret for now :)


[h3]BATTLE REPORT[/h3]

Now, when you leave the conflict map, you will be presented with a report screen showing your performance during the conflict. This screen is still in the early stages of development, but you can currently view important statistics.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43756138/ce941a970a9ce21763d247575086065551e79bf8.jpg[/img]

These include the number of enemy ships you have destroyed, the number of asteroids or other objects you have scanned, the number of fighters you have lost, and the amount of ammunition you have used.

[b]A new way to make money
[/b]
You can also earn a small amount of money by selling information to local mining companies about the asteroids you scanned on the conflict map that were still intact when you left the map. Keep this in mind...

notes.title: Development Blog: Trading with planets and stations
notes.content:
The trading system, the infrastructure of which we have been building for a long time, is now actively working in the developer version. The interface and final tests for the update are nearing completion.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43756138/8f0b80a55fe13debe5a3de0ac0ba9504fa39d110.jpg[/img]

[h3]So when is the update coming?[/h3]

If all goes well and the tests show no problems, we plan to release the update this week.

[h3]What will you be doing after the update?[/h3]

Our new development plan includes the implementation of equipment other than weapons. Engines, combat computers, technological accessories, mods, armour, etc. This equipment will give both the mothership and the fighters very different tactical capabilities.

For example, we are aware that many of our players complain that the Father moves "slowly". In this case, you will need an engine that will give this giant body more thrust. In fact, in later updates, you will need to find the right engineering officers to make your engines more effective and develop them through training.

Or, if you complain that your mini-turrets are slow to fire, a skilled Tactical Officer who can modify them to fire faster can make your life a lot easier during conflicts.

In Pirate Patrol, which uses procedural generation technology, it is up to you to come up with creative solutions to every problem.

Thank you for your support during the game's Early Access period, which gave us the courage to create an extraordinary and immersive tactics/strategy game.

notes.title: Update v.0.6.3 : Stations, debris, logistics, exploration
notes.content:
With the v.0.6.3 update, Pirate Patrol now encourages players to explore.

On the game's battle map, you can find asteroids, abandoned space stations that have turned into ruins, or old spaceships that have been defeated in battles and lost in the darkness of space. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43756138/ffe4cbf343a23cd948b98203cc8b489e9a7942ca.png[/img]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43756138/e212674ed509a609121a1c5c815773e8f66e273d.png[/img]

Scanning all of these items will give you XP, but you can also find useful technology from the debris.

Scanning asteroids is also important for understanding the movements and orbits of these giant rocks in the mothership's path and avoiding collisions. The Father will no longer collide with scanned asteroids.

[b]Logistics issues[/b]
All weapons in your cargo now have a recycle value. You can send these items for recycling by pressing the recycle button on The Father's configuration screen, and the useful materials obtained from recycling will be stored in The Father's logistics hangars. As you know, these logistics warehouses produce ammunition for your turrets and fighters. So it would be a wise move to recycle unused loads to keep your warehouses ready for battle.

[b]Damage control and repair[/b]
In previous versions, we could only repair damage done to The Father when we entered a planet's orbit. You can now initiate a repair operation on your ship at any time using the icon that appears at the bottom of the bridge panel. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43756138/d3306acca46a00b93f355eb913441f17ccdcaae6.png[/img]

However, this repair will be done using materials from your [b]logistics stores[/b], and will not be as [b]effective [/b]as a full repair in planet or station orbit. However, being able to repair your damaged main ship after heavy clashes is a very important strategic advantage.

There are now [b]space stations[/b] in the game, and you can repair and resupply both in planetary orbit and in space stations.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43756138/01d095ffec7662aebf2f377c340ac47412d1c49c.png[/img]

[b]Control Interface[/b]
At the request of our players, we have also made some changes to the game's control interface.

We can now give collective attack/scan/move orders to the ships we select by dragging with the mouse.

[list]
[*] [b]All fighters can be selected and released using keyboard keys 1-5.
[*] All turrets can be selected and released with SHIFT + 1-5.[/b]
[/list]

If you want to select multiple ships on the fighter panel and give them collective orders, simply press the sections on the panel to turn the selection light green. From now on, when you give an order (attack/scan/move), all ships with a green selection light will obey your order.

[b]Enemy ships[/b]
We did not diversify the enemy ships enough in the previous part of the alpha phase. You will now encounter a large number of enemy fighters with very different characteristics. Here are a few examples:

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43756138/f1aa26eb0548ad929034bb5d724a9c620b66d9c5.png[/img]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43756138/ea127460038dfd74534b0e775effc4975efb0532.png[/img]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43756138/525d2e1fcfb0e00b8852f9989d549efcef4b3064.png[/img]

[b]And leveling up[/b]
The leveling mechanism has been in the game for a long time, but we never announced it to the players. We tried to make the leveling system different from the usual classic systems. However, our most observant players noticed that as they fought enemies, they gained XP and their level in the character panel increased.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43756138/df51f4c794b411bbea169a80265ee388dc8c68b4.png[/img]

Currently, we define the level system as the degree of operational security that the Federal Intelligence Service provides to the player. As your level increases, you will be able to integrate more effective combat equipment into your ship and combat gear. For example, the armour and weapons of your fighter ships will become stronger, etc. We will continue to develop this system and present it in its full form in the game. But for now, you can get approval from the FIS for higher operational contributions by earning XP when you fight the enemy or conduct reconnaissance.

notes.title: Update for enhance quality of life
notes.content:
[h3]1.Scan and Loot[/h3]
With our new update, we have disabled the "icon" clicking issue that caused problems with Scan and Loot. Now all you have to do is select the fighter to scan or loot and right-click on the shipwreck to be scanned or the find to be looted.


[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43756138/85bf6c017350573406cc7fd793437c5fc6cabec9.png[/img]

[h3]2.Select Fighters and Turrets with Num Keys
[/h3]
With this update, you can now select fighters and turrets with the number keys.

To select fighters, you can use the [b]1,2,3,4 and 5 keys[/b]. This order depends on which BAY the fighter is assigned to. Number 1 for fighter in BAY 1, number 5 for fighter in BAY 5... Also, during combat, you can see the pilot's name and BAY number of the fighter under the Fighter sprite.

To select the Turrets, you now had to press the Turret number with the [b]+SHIFT key.[/b] In previous versions, Turrets could only be selected by pressing the 1,2,3,4,5 keys, but after the auto-fire feature, the fire control of mini turrets was largely automated. You can use combinations of [b]SHIFT+3[/b] for the Large Turret and SHIFT+6 and SHIFT+7 for the Missile launchers. You can also select these turrets by left-clicking on the Mothership, or you can open the Turrets panel and click on the relevant turret's panel. This way you can select them and have them ready for target selection.



[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43756138/2da4073e38ce6fda2b81263768bb84d17d3c4e3d.png[/img]


[h3]3. Recall all fighters to the mothership[/h3]
Among the fighter control buttons, there is now a "Recall All" button in the 3rd row to call all fighters in space to the mother ship at once. When you press this, all fighters on duty in space will return to the mother ship. We believe that this is a button that will make the job of our players much easier after conflicts and collecting loot.

As our experienced players will notice, there are no Scan and Loot buttons in the button row anymore. As we explained in the first title, you can now automatically start the scan and loot process by right-clicking on shipwrecks.

***
Some small reminders:

[b]Level:
[/b]
We see that some of our players have not yet noticed the Levels of friendly and enemy warriors. The game awards XP to Captain Lionheart and fighter pilots every time you destroy an enemy ship. This is not yet noticeable, but in the following battles you may encounter enemies of much different levels. You can see the Levels of your friendly warriors at the top of the fighter sprite. If you are going to attack a very high level enemy, we recommend that you organize your fighters as a team, because high level enemies can be strong enough to cause heavy damage even to the mother ship, and of course, they can cut your fighters's armors like paper.

[b]Pilot priorities:[/b]
You should not expect the pilots under your command to strictly obey your every command. If these NPC pilots, under the control of artificial intelligence, sense an emergency, they may decide to abandon their mission and intervene in this emergency. For example, you may have tasked a pilot with scanning enemy debris. However, one of his comrades may have been under heavy enemy attack at that time. In this case, the NPC pilot may choose to abandon the scan mission you gave and run to the aid of his friend. In many situations like this, you may witness pilots leaving your command by analyzing the situation around them. Don't panic, you can try giving orders to your pilots until they accept your authority. But we don't know if it will work. Artificial intelligence's mind can work differently.


We wish you hours of fun in the game and we welcome your feedback.

notes.title: Update v.o.6.2f: Missille control
notes.content:
With the new update, we have released the core of the Missile Weapon System, which will add significant tactical richness to the game.

This update brings the following changes to rocket weapons

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43756138/82f942f83fe00f53c8f1c47a4c96b44a61de4a56.gif[/img]
[b][h3]1. New vertical missile launchers[/h3][/b]
We have updated the mothership missile launcher. Instead of the 360-degree rotating ground attack vehicle type launcher on the FATHER, there is now a naval vertical launcher.

[b][h3]2. Launching many missiles at once[/h3][/b]
You can now take advantage of a "multi-barrelled" missile launcher when launching a missile attack from the mothership. It is possible to launch up to 5 missiles at the same time. You can adjust this using the + and - buttons on the missile launchers in the turret panel. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43756138/5dad6838f2d23a2e7f0bb1afdd312bb80c4314a4.gif[/img]

If you set the number of missiles to be fired to 0, the launcher will stop firing at the target, but will continue to track it. This is particularly important to avoid wasting valuable missiles on enemy ships hiding in the dense asteroid field.

[previewyoutube=Wjbh4sFG0rg;full][/previewyoutube]

[h3][b]3. Missiles are expensive toys[/b][/h3]
It is important to remember that missiles are expensive weapons. You can quickly deplete your ship's ammunition by firing large numbers of missiles at worthless targets, making you an easy target in the middle of a battle with weapons that cannot fire. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43756138/c3669398e05602de3b07e7237f242d4107204264.gif[/img]

However, high-level, especially heavy-class enemy drones are capable of inflicting serious damage on both the Father and your fighters in a very short time. As a practical option, you may want to consider sending multiple missiles at once to quickly destroy these heavy enemy fighters.

[b][h3]4. Enemies hunt missiles![/h3][/b]
Enemy ships now have the ability to destroy incoming missiles by shooting them down. This can mean that your valuable missiles are easily destroyed. So if you are launching missiles at enemy ships, you may want to try to  catch them in positions where they cannot hit the missiles.

[b][h3]5. Missile attack with fighters[/h3][/b]
In the previous update, we reduced the number of fighter missiles from 30 to 16. Missile attacks on both motherships and fighters now have an ammo cost. Missile attacks on the mothership will consume ammunition from the mothership's depots as soon as they are fired. Fighters, on the other hand, go on missions by loading their missile weapons. When they return to the hangar, the missing missiles are replaced, using up the resources in the mothership's ammunition depot. Meanwhile, missile attacks by fighters are less costly.


We look forward to hearing your comments.

notes.title: A letter from the developers
notes.content:
As developers who spent our childhoods reading sci-fi novels such as Randevous with Rama, Dune, Starship Troopers, The Martian Chronicles, in the years before the Internet was discovered, we were aware that we were embarking on a difficult path when we started developing Pirate Patrol, and we have not regretted it, we have enjoyed every stage of this work.

Of course, when we come across a fantasy RPG, we enjoy swinging swords and throwing fireballs, battling dragons in Skyrim, replaying Divinity Original Sin 2 with different teammates, reliving the excitement of building a kingdom in Pathfinder: Kingmaker, or we never get tired of boarding our sailing pirate ship and boarding enemy ships in Pillars of Eternity II: Deadfire...

However, when it comes to sci-fi, things stop for us. Although we are aware that science fiction is possible with a creative imagination, we are among those who believe that the "science" part of the work imposes a responsibility on any science fiction work.

[h3][b]Fireballs in Science Fiction
[/b][/h3]
To take a very simple example, a fantasy roleplaying game wouldn't question the wizard's ability to create and throw a fireball in the palm of his hand. However, if a character in a science fiction story creates a fireball in the palm of his hand and throws it left and right, the science fiction reader/player will want to see a scientific explanation for this. So science fiction stories explain that characters can create a fireball by drawing energy from perhaps another dimension, perhaps with the various accessories/devices they wear. Of course, this is one of the simplest examples...

As we develop Pirate Patrol, we keep in mind our goal to appeal to science fiction fans. At the same time, we want you to have fun playing the game we have created. For this reason, we apologise to our players who are tired of seeing long texts in some parts of the game. This is partly due to our "sci-fi" obsession and our desire to get the story straight to the player.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43756138/b79c6fa5f0ea2d27d89e49c6d2535126d27d9348.jpg[/img]

With the new update, which will be released in the coming days,[/url] we will now be able to configure fighters and remove the long text sections at the beginning of the game, allowing the player to quickly get into the game and the action. The "long text at the beginning" that some of our players complained about has been spread out so that it appears in different parts of the game, bit by bit.

[h3][b]Play it fast or play it slow?
[/b][/h3]
On the other hand, we would like to remind you that Pirate Patrol is actually a tactical RPG designed to be played "slowly". 

Although it is not a big problem to play the game "fast" at this stage, our players will notice that the features we add in each update make tactical control more important in the game. In the final version, our players will have to make critical decisions in conflicts by pausing the game or reducing the speed of the [b]Neural Network[/b] to "tactical" level. 

For example, while fighters are out in space scanning for new technologies in enemy debris, there is a risk that flying asteroids will come fast and hit the debris, destroying it. Therefore, the player may need to protect these debris piles and hunt for asteroids with both the surrounding fighters and the mother ship's weapons.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43756138/8a48b59b3f4d54ae23ab40a44b1e049b54440ffc.jpg[/img]

Especially after the introduction of the fighter configuration update, making tactical decisions in the game will become even more important. 

For example, the missile you load onto a fighter can reach much higher speeds than normal missiles. Since the missiles fired by other fighters will not be able to hit a very fast moving robot fighter, you may want to order the fighters you have specially loaded with "fast missiles" to attack this "fast" enemy.

Let's take another example. Soon enemy ships will be launching missiles, and enemy missiles will pose a great risk to both fighters and the FATHER. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43756138/a0dc6b2f5edfc9cb9ac49b106a1e36b7f06f585f.png[/img]

The FATHER's point defence weapons will be able to destroy these enemy missiles, but if there are a large number of missiles, your fighters may need to hunt them down. In this case, if you have assigned your fighters to pilots with very strong piloting skills, who can move very fast and have powerful engines, and if you have equipped these fighters with long-range weapons that can fire very quickly, your job will be very easy. So you need to pause or slow down the conflict and choose and assign your "suitable" fighters.

For players who don't want to bother with these tactical decisions, the game will continue. Artificial intelligence pilots and officers will still find a way to destroy the "fast" robot ship. However, in the meantime, your mothership will have taken more damage, you will have burned more ammunition, your resources will have been more depleted, your valuable fighters may have taken more damage and will have to return to the mothership for repairs, leaving you vulnerable for a while. Each choice will have a different outcome.

To sum up, we put a lot of effort into making Pirate Patrol a game that offers a lot of options for sci-fi lovers and has a solid logical infrastructure. We are having a lot of fun and hope you enjoy the game. Thank you all for supporting Pirate Patrol during this development process.

notes.title: It's time to loot!
notes.content:
We have reached a certain level in the main modules of Pirate Patrol and it's time to implement the looting system. 

With the new update, you can now scan the remains of enemy ships to see what parts/technologies you can salvage, and then use your small ships to loot the technologies you want to take back to your main ship. 

For now, only weapons that can be used on the mothership will be dropped from enemy ships. We hope that our friends playing and testing the game in Early Access will enjoy the experience more.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43756138/997a499e13d2d4a7844ebbbdfd7429b63f7afa5f.png[/img]

However, new loot types will be implemented in the near future. Engines, consoles, missile technologies, war computers, technologies that can be used on the mothership or fighter ships...

[b]ASTEROIDS[/b]
You must also take special care to protect the shipwrecks and loot crates that roam space.

Shipwrecks will disappear into the dark void of space after a while if you do not scan them.

Like shipwrecks, loot crates are very sensitive to asteroid impacts, and the new addition of moving asteroids will cause them to explode if they hit shipwrecks or loot crates as they move around the map like a loose cannon. After all, we are talking about asteroids travelling through space at high speeds. Nothing is more common than hitting another object and causing heavy damage. This is why we recommend that you protect shipwrecks and loot crates from asteroids. 

[b]There are 3 main tactics you can use to do this.
[/b]
1. The main ship's turret can shoot asteroids approaching the wreck from a distance. If the asteroid is heading towards a wreck or a loot crate, you should take immediate action.

2. You can send your fighter ships to shoot/hunt these asteroids. And yes, fighter ships can now attack asteroids. Simply select one or more fighters (using drag select) and left-click on the asteroid you want to attack.

3. Tiny moving asteroids cannot damage The Father's special alloy armour. You can therefore use your mothership as a shield against asteroids, while your fighters have time to scan and loot the debris.


[b]"HELP"[/b]

With the new update, we have also updated the 'Help' section in the 'Settings' menu, where you can find little tips and tricks to help you play the game. We encourage you to take a look.

notes.title: Update v.0.6: Crew and Fighters
notes.content:
Pirate Patrol now has more tactical options. As we continue to develop the game in Early Access, we have released the Crew and Fighters update for our friends who want to give the game a try. 

With this update, you will be able to choose the pilots and officers that will serve under your command on the mothership at the beginning of the game. You will also be able to choose the fighter ships that you will place on your mothership from the list created for you by the Federal Intelligence Service and have them transported to your ship.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43756138/eeb3dcb746f8a945eaea90e0eff17b4d1677f1fa.jpg[/img]

All pilots and fighters have their own unique characteristics. Therefore, you should consider the following criteria when making your selection. Some pilots have a better command of their fighters and can fly their ships under intense enemy fire without taking damage, some are skilled at making their ships go faster, and some are more skilled at inflicting critical damage because they know their enemies better.  

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43756138/d653eb80cf22b1087c82ae732082b8016db60986.jpg[/img]

Similarly, the fighters you transfer to the mother ship vary in speed, HP, sensor range, and attack factor, all of which, when combined with the skills of the pilots on the battlefield, create very different tactical options for a commander.

With this update, we've also made improvements to the game's sounds, music, and some visual elements. For example, you'll now love the battle soundtrack, or when your long-range heavy artillery hits an enemy ship, even if it doesn't destroy it, it can cause it to lose its balance and spin around. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43756138/80ce29e9dcf3b52e42e51d17c1a715ca03c5288e.jpg[/img]

As we've [url=https://store.steampowered.com/news/app/2339490/view/4179973693312651984?snr=1___]already announced[/url], we'll be introducing loot and item crafting features in another update in March. So you'll be able to customize the weapons on the mothership and the fighter ships, and load each weapon with different projectiles or missiles and get different effects. 

We are working hard to improve Pirate Patrol and thank you all for your support.

notes.title: PRE-RPG UPDATE
notes.content:
We have opened the interface that will form the basis of the RPG system to comments from our players.

With the v.0.5-Alpha update, we're unveiling the interface for the detailed and deep RPG system we have planned for Pirate Patrol.


[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43756138/79321dd8f69dc02b2f2da92677d73b8a4b714de8.jpg[/img]

At the moment, the interface works mechanically, as Captain Lionheart gains XP, you can see the progress on the character panel, but character screen features such as skill selection are not available. 

Also, for now, this interface only shows the character screen for Captain Lionheart, but there will be separate character screens for each pilot and officer in the game. But first, we want to clarify the interface design with feedback from our players.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43756138/e29770389b907f229ceace42de420011c5bac223.jpg[/img]

We are also focusing on skills. For now, we have only created visuals of 11 skills to test the interface, but in the next updates, when the RPG system is fully implemented, there will be hundreds of different skills. As players level up, they will be able to unlock the appropriate skills, but there will also be hidden skills that can be obtained by completing quests, trading, or exploring different parts of the universe. 

[b]Speaking of exploration...[/b]

At Pirate Patrol, we believe that exploration is a powerful gameplay motivator. For this reason, we are working on a galaxy map that is 10 times larger and we will release this new map in the next updates.

Of course, we are also preparing the myriad of factions, pirate gangs, political entities, colonies, wealthy merchants, trading, competing, fighting, missions, etc. that will fill this huge map.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43756138/9f912c1f9b533ee71fe71d3bc85e38888efa88fb.jpg[/img]

[b]TOP MENU [/b]

A new element we have added to the visual design of the game is the TOP MENU, which appears in the top right corner. This menu allows you to access panels that were previously only accessible using the keyboard shortcuts, by clicking on them with the mouse. These are:

[olist]
[*] Character Panel (P) 
[*] Hangar Panel (H) 
[*] Galaxy Map (G) 
[*] Settings Menu (ESC)
[/olist]

Thank you for your support of the game. We continue to work hard to make Pirate Patrol a very immersive and deep RPG. We would love to hear your comments in the Steam Discussions section.

notes.title: Pirate Patrol is now more playable
notes.content:
When we released the game to Early Access, we recommended a screen resolution of 1920x1080 pixels. While that's pretty much standard in the gaming world right now, we're aware that some of our friends are using different resolutions. We noticed that these players were experiencing breaks in the GUI design and seeing 2 mouse pointers during combat. With the new update, we've fixed this problem. Now, even those who don't use 1920x1080 resolution can play the game without encountering the 2 mouse pointer problem. 

Of course, if your monitor does not support 1920x1080 resolution, we recommend that you select a 16:9 screen resolution. This will give you a smoother gaming experience.

In addition to fixing this bug, we have also made improvements in the following areas to make life easier for players:

1. The "target" pointer on enemy ships now also shows how many turrets are aimed at them. This allows you to see more clearly on the tactical screen which enemy ships you should be focusing your firepower on and which targets you should be targeting. 

2. Fixed some display issues in the hangar panel and galaxy map panel.

3. We added a new mouse cursor to the game, which provides a more comfortable view.

4. We added a speech bubble to the dialogs of warriors who are damaged in battle and call for help, so you can see their dialogs more clearly.

5. To make it easier to recognize new distress signals when patrolling the galaxy map, we have added voice alerts. Our ship's officers will now verbally alert us when they receive a new distress signal.

6. We have redesigned the turret panel on the tactical map to make the data on it easier to read. It is now easier to see which turret has targeted which enemy and which turret has no target. Also, when you click on a targeted enemy in the turret panel, the weapon's lock on that enemy disappears.

7. In the fighter panel, you can see the fighters that are not on a mission and docked in the hangar, or those that are on a mission in space, making them easier to select.

[b]Next Updates:[/b]

Thank you for supporting Pirate Patrol in Early Access. We are excited to work on integrating the RPG system into the game in upcoming updates. You can read our news on this topic at this link:

[url=https://store.steampowered.com/news/app/2339490/view/3871471412523428252]https://store.steampowered.com/news/app/2339490/view/3871471412523428252[/url]
